A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, three figures, seven tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and explanation-evaluation results for four LLMs across four datasets in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–3, including definition-permutation, perturbation, and integration experiments.

M1.justification: The definition-permutation and perturbation procedures and four integration conditions remain unchanged, including k-NN generation of adjusted definitions. Added scope explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate e-SNLI, WELLXPLAIN, HATEXPLAIN, and WICE with the same tasks and definition scenarios. Generation, reasoning, and disputed definitions are discussed as future work, without additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same models and comparison conditions. Mistral is relabeled Mistral-7B; Table 5 identifies the same checkpoint in both versions.

E3.justification: Both specify the same GPT-4 sampling policy, full test sets for other models, retrieval k values, dataset splits, and MCC/ROUGE/F1 evaluation. The copyedited illustrative examples in Table 4 do not establish an experimental setting change.

E4.justification: The permutation, definition-quality, integration comparisons, and illustrated cases are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis appears; attention analysis is only discussed as future work.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. Section 4.1 corrects the reported WICE trend for LLaMA-3 and Mistral from 'no improvement at all' to 'marginal improvement,' matching the retained increases of 0.09 to 0.13 and 0.03 to 0.05.

T1.justification: The permutation construction, mean misaligned MCC, piecewise WICE F1 formula, and adjusted-definition expression are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, four key insights, and principal conclusions remain substantively unchanged. Added remarks about broader tasks and disputed definitions are framed as possible extensions and future work.

C2.justification: v3 explains the classification focus, distinguishes legitimately disputed definitions from erroneous ones, and explains why attention-weight analysis was omitted. Section 4.2 replaces the pretraining-based interpretation of stable WICE F1 with an explanation tied to claim–evidence matching.

D1.justification: Model identifiers and parameter counts, retrieval settings, the prompt template, appendix label definitions, dataset statistics, and code-access information are retained. Table 4 reformats and copyedits existing examples without adding implementation information.

R1.justification: v3 adds four references supporting the attention-analysis limitation, replaces Matthews (1975) with Baldi et al. (2000) for MCC, and removes the Lin et al. (2024) citation from the WICE discussion. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain scope and limitations, expand acknowledgments, and repeat the contribution summary in Section 5. Model names, cross-references, and bibliographic details are edited, while the overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 changes from stacked example blocks to Premise/Hypothesis/Label columns. Figure 2 and Table 1 are relocated, model typography changes, and captions are revised, especially Table 3. The same figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves precision through clearer scope boundaries, the corrected WICE trend description, and a more task-grounded explanation of WICE F1 stability. Table 4 is easier to compare visually. These gains are limited by redundant contribution prose and remaining inaccuracies, including the unchanged claim that Phi-3 declines when Table 2 shows an increase from 0.01 to 0.05.
